legs.name: clippy
legs.extract: select(.reason == "compiler-message") | select(.message.level == "error" or .message.level == "warning") | {type: "clippy", level: .message.level, file: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].file_name // .message.spans[0]?.file_name // "unknown"), line: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].line_start // .message.spans[0]?.line_start // null), lint: (.message.code.code // "compile-error"), message: .message.message}

legs.name: blocking-call-in-native-bif
legs.note: Wrapped in a script because the BARE `ast-grep scan` returns its PASSING verdict (empty findings, rc 0) in two failure states, both measured: an emptied rule pattern list, and a scan path that does not exist -- the latter prints 'No such file or directory' to STDERR while still exiting 0, so even capturing stderr does not fail the leg. A missing rule FILE does exit nonzero (rc 6) and was already safe. beamr has restructured src/ directories twice recently, so a renamed native/ would have left this gate scanning nothing and reporting clean forever. The script establishes that the checker CAN fire (positive-control fixtures under .ast-grep/fixtures/, requiring one hit per declared pattern, so an untested new pattern fails the gate) and that the scan path exists and holds >=1 .rs file, BEFORE believing an empty result. Line numbers in ast-grep's --json output are ZERO-INDEXED while its human report style is one-indexed: a finding printed as line 212 appears as "line": 211 here. Do not chase a phantom off-by-one. The script parses the JSON count rather than trusting exit codes, and never suppresses stderr -- the 'N error(s) found' notice during the positive control is EXPECTED and is announced on the line above it.

legs.name: clippy-all-features
legs.extract: select(.reason == "compiler-message") | select(.message.level == "error" or .message.level == "warning") | {type: "clippy", level: .message.level, file: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].file_name // .message.spans[0]?.file_name // "unknown"), line: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].line_start // .message.spans[0]?.line_start // null), lint: (.message.code.code // "compile-error"), message: .message.message}
legs.note: ADDED because the canon compiled exactly ONE feature combination and a whole module tree escaped it. `telemetry` is enabled by NOBODY -- not beamr-cli (default), not beamr-wasm (default-features=false, cooperative+json), not the sibling clippy leg's `--features beamr/encode`, not dev-dependencies -- yet `#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")] pub mod telemetry;` gates four files and 156 cfg sites. MEASURED, not argued: a deliberate TYPE error planted in telemetry/spans.rs passed all six then-legs (fmt 0, clippy 0, wasm32-check 0, wasm-tests 0, tests 0, blocking-call 0), while `cargo check -p beamr --features telemetry` returned rc 101 naming exactly that line. The specimen was a TYPE error and not a syntax error on purpose: rustfmt walks `mod` declarations syntactically and ignores #[cfg], so a syntax error would have gone red at the fmt leg for a reason that is not the claim. `--all-features` rather than an enumerated `--features a,b,c` so a NEWLY DECLARED feature is covered by construction -- an enumerated list is a second copy of the feature set and drifts the first time somebody adds a feature and forgets this line. THIS LEG DOES NOT REPLACE ITS SIBLING and must not be collapsed into it: every cfg has a complement, so under --all-features all `#[cfg(not(feature = ...))]` code stops being compiled, and `not(feature = "threads")` is how the cooperative runtime is selected. The canon therefore compiles THREE named combinations on purpose -- default-union-encode (sibling clippy/tests legs, the shape host consumers build), cooperative+json with default-features=false (the wasm32-check leg, which is the only leg that type-checks the not-threads paths), and all-on (this leg, the only leg that compiles telemetry). Three named points out of 2^14 is NOT 'every feature combination is gated'; read a green canon as exactly those three and no more.

legs.name: tests-all-features
legs.note: ADDED once green. #97 declared this leg known-red and deliberately withheld it rather than quietly dropping it: cargo test --workspace --all-features was 1838 passed / 4 failed, all four telemetry-gated scheduler::tests, failing identically under --test-threads=1 so NOT the parallel-run OTel flake. #98 resolved it at 3c1e08f. The cause was neither of the two candidates on the board: all four entered at instruction_pointer 0, which in their module layout is the FuncInfo instruction -- the multi-clause dispatch LANDING PAD, which since 5bcd529 (shipped 0.16.3) raises a catchable error:function_clause instead of continuing. shutdown was irrelevant, proven by removing it and getting byte-identical outcomes; and there is no scheduler fairness defect, proven by entering one instruction later and getting the asserted Requeue. Production never had the bug because Scheduler::spawn_in resolves label_ip and enters after the pad. THIS LEG IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE tests LEG: its sibling runs --features beamr/encode and compiles NO telemetry code, so these four tests -- the only direct execute_slice call sites in the tree -- were executed by nothing at all until this leg existed. That is the same reach hole clippy-all-features was added for, one layer down: clippy-all-features proves telemetry COMPILES, this leg proves it RUNS. Do not collapse the two, and do not read a green here as covering feature combinations beyond all-on.

legs.name: nostd-ratchet
legs.note: ADDED because a WAIVED gate with no ratchet is a number that only ever grows. `cargo check -p beamr --no-default-features` is red and its redness is deliberately waived (CHANGELOG.md and docs/DIST-CONTROL-WIRE-SPEC.md both record it as "waived, not green"; restoring no-std is a separate work item, brief B-144). The waiver was honest. What nothing recorded is that the number MOVED: rustc's own tally says 1019 errors at ec5d7f8 (2026-07-07) and 1039 at d4a82e5 (2026-08-16) -- +20 across five minor versions, unremarked. Measured at both pins with the same instrument and the same error composition (E0433/E0425-dominated), so it is drift and not an artifact of building an old commit under a newer toolchain. COUNTING RULE, and it has already caught two seats: use rustc's own "due to N previous errors" line. Do NOT count `^error` lines -- the trailing `error: could not compile ...` summary line is itself an `error` line, so a naive grep reads exactly one too many. The historical record's "1020" and the first reading of "1040" in this lane are both that same off-by-one against rustc's 1019/1039; neither was wrong about the world. Whenever a figure from this leg is quoted beside a historical one, STATE THE RECONCILIATION or the next reader concludes a seat miscounted. WHY THE DRIFT WAS INVISIBLE -- two structural halves, neither sufficient alone: the waiver lived in PROSE, unwatchable; and `--no-default-features` is INERT under `cargo test`, because crates/beamr/Cargo.toml's dev-dependency on beamr ITSELF carries default features and cargo unifies features across graph edges, so the flag binds the command-line package while the dev edge still asks for `default = true`. No test-shaped gate could ever have selected the configuration. That manifest edge is its own lane -- fixing it changes what every `cargo test` builds. THIS LEG IS STRICT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON PURPOSE: an IMPROVEMENT also fails, demanding the ceiling be lowered in the same commit, because slack in a ratchet is room to drift back up to it silently. It REFUSES (rc 3) rather than passing when the tally line is absent, since a green from an instrument that could not measure is worth nothing. `--self-test` proves all seven arms fire.
